prerequisites: It is recommended to have successfully completed the courses Fluid Mechanics, Fluid Machinery and Installations, and Industrial Flow Simulation.

learning_outcomes.text: That students have the ability to gather and interpret relevant data (normally within their field of study) to make judgments that include reflection on relevant social, scientific or ethical issues.

That students have demonstrated possession and understanding of knowledge in a field of study that builds on general secondary education, and is usually found at a level that, while supported by advanced textbooks, also includes some aspects that imply knowledge from the forefront of their field of study.
That students have developed the learning skills necessary to undertake further studies with a high degree of autonomy.

That students know how to apply their knowledge to their work or vocation in a professional way and possess the competencies that are usually demonstrated through the elaboration and defense of arguments and the resolution of problems within their field of study.
That students can transmit information, ideas, problems and solutions to both specialized and non-specialized audiences.
Applied knowledge of the fundamentals of fluid-mechanical systems and machines.
Ability to work, lead and manage conflicts in a multidisciplinary group and/or a multilingual environment.
Ability to apply new technologies including information and communication technologies.
Ability to manage information, handle and apply technical specifications and legislation necessary for engineering practice.
Knowledge of the basic principles of fluid mechanics and its application to solving problems in the field of engineering. Calculation of pipes, channels and fluid systems.
Basic knowledge about the use and programming of computers, operating systems, databases and computer programs with application in engineering.

syllabus_topics: Hydraulic power plants. Water hammer. Surge tanks
History. Classification of wind systems. Applications. Economic aspects
The Wind: Wind resource. Wind maps. ABL. Convective cell. Wind variation scale. Profiles. Turbulence
Aerodynamics: Fundamentals. Component. Wings. Actuator disk. Rotor-disk system. Rotor-blade system. Influence of number of blades.
Practice: Analysis and design of surge tanks for water hammer in power plants
Practice: Aerodynamics of a free-rotating wind turbine
Practice: Realistic evaluation of wind resource and wind farm design
teaching_methods: Theory explanation and general examples discussion
Solving engineering problems using GIS and mathematical/CFD software
Analysis of a problem of interest in wind energy and discussion in small groups

assessment_methods.method: Attendance and/or participation in in-person and/or virtual activities
Theoretical concepts of the subject (written test)
Completion of assignments, cases or exercises (individual work)

assessment_rules: The grading system will be governed by RD 1125/2003 of September 5, which establishes the European credit system and the grading system in official university degrees. Continuous assessment will be favored and preferably adopted where appropriate. A grade equal to or higher than 5 out of 10 must be obtained in the computerized/written test (aspect S2). Attendance and evaluation of practices will be carried out by attendance control and delivery of a report with the solution to the problems (aspect S4). An individual/collective assignment must be submitted with a detailed and well-presented solution (aspect S3).
